pattern.crimePattern: a committee chairwoman sedates and smothers a county auditor who found a falsified child death record, then stages a desert breakdown
pattern.notes: Fictional people, guesthouse, dispensary and committee. The child's death a year ago is told only in a register, a clinical note and a referral form, in report language, and never shown. Open decision for the user: the child death in the back-story (see the region report). Spine background: Abdia Golicha's letter about the "digitisation" man (t_registry); Abdia is the victim of case 80.

ob.reportedBy: A camel herder, by radio from Kalacha mission
ob.text: A camel herder reports a county vehicle stuck in the sand 8 km out in the Chalbi desert from Kalacha, and a woman dead in its shade: Ubah Osman (38), Marsabit county public-health officer. Suspected death from heat after a breakdown.

facts.text: Ubah Osman was found dead beside a county car stuck 8 km out in the Chalbi on Friday morning; heat after a breakdown is suspected.
The county car is sunk to its axles in soft sand; Ubah lay in its shade.
The driver's seat is pushed far forward. Ubah was 1.78 m tall: there is no way she drove with the seat there.
Her cash float, KSh 23,000, is still in the glovebox.
Halake: someone dying of heat beside a stuck car drinks her water, and digs.
On the back seat: two 5-litre water bottles, full and sealed.
There is no digging under the wheels and no branches; the sand ladders are still on the roof. Ubah had done a desert-driving course.
Ewoi: no footprints of Ubah's around the car; one set of an older woman's sandals, short stride, worn heel, from the driver's door back towards Kalacha. The night before last.
Ubah's audit draft, Wednesday 19:10: "Kalacha: one child death misrecorded. Report to OCS Marsabit Thursday."
A letter from Abdia Golicha, Isiolo land registry: a man from Nairobi is "digitising" the registry; files go into his boxes and don't come back. She is keeping her own list.
Guesthouse register: Ubah checked in on Tuesday. No check-out, no payment.
In Ubah's room: the bed made up tight, two pillows with no cases, her suitcase still under the bed.
Death register, a year ago: "Diba Elema, 6 — fell from a donkey cart — dead on arrival", in Peter Langat's hand.
Peter's clinical notes, the same night: "Crush injuries chest and pelvis; consistent with vehicle; mother says the water truck."
The referral form copy for Diba Elema gives the cause as "fall", signed P. Langat.
Under raking light: the cause box first read "RTA" (road traffic accident); it was overwritten as "fall" in a different ink.
Bowser log: Arero drove the bowser to North Horr at 16:00 on Wednesday and returned at 12:10 on Thursday.
Sister Agnes: at 03:40 on Thursday, ringing for night prayer, she saw a woman in a white headscarf walking in from the Chalbi, slowly.
Sister Agnes was at the mission all night with the other sisters.
Sister Agnes: Peter sat up all night at the dispensary with a feverish child and her mother; she took them soup at midnight.
Records: Ubah's phone stayed on the Kalacha mast until 01:08 on Thursday, when it left coverage moving east. She made no call after 20:30 on Wednesday.
Shanko's sandals: worn heels, the Chalbi's white sand in the treads.
In Shanko's house: a sleeping-tablet strip in her name, six missing, filled last week.
One pillowcase, washed, drying on Shanko's line.
North Horr customers: Arero delivered water there on Wednesday night and slept by the bowser.
The elders: Elema was with his family and herds 30 km away; he accepted the settlement a year ago and never met Ubah.
Post-mortem: not heatstroke. Small bleeding spots in the eyes and bruising inside the lips: smothering.
Post-mortem: death on Wednesday night between 23:00 and 01:00, before the car reached the desert.
Lab: a sedative in Ubah's blood matching Shanko's prescription.
Lab: the sandal prints by the car match Shanko's sandals.
Lab: the lint in Ubah's nose matches the washed pillowcase.
Missing: her water bottles are full and there's no digging at the wheels.
Missing: there are no footprints of hers around the car.
Missing: she made no call for help.
Missing: there's no dehydration in the body.
Missing: there's no check-out in the register.

reconstruction.text: A year ago, at dusk, Arero's bowser hits six-year-old Diba Elema at the watering point. Shanko settles with the family through the elders, in camels, and pays Peter Langat KSh 50,000 to change the referral form from "RTA" to "fall".
This week Ubah Osman audits child deaths. On Wednesday she compares the register with Peter's notes and the referral form, and at 19:10 drafts: "Report to OCS Marsabit Thursday."
At dinner she tells Shanko. Shanko crushes six of her sleeping tablets into Ubah's camel milk. At about 23:30, with Ubah asleep, she smothers her with a pillow.
At 01:00 she puts Ubah in the passenger seat, pulls the driver's seat forward and drives 8 km into the Chalbi. She runs the car into soft sand, lays Ubah in its shade, and walks home under the stars.
At 03:40 Sister Agnes, ringing for night prayer, sees a woman in a white headscarf walking in from the desert. In the morning Shanko washes one pillowcase.
